battle.name: 薩米安戰爭
battle.brief: 前440年，薩米斯島寡頭垮台後求助米利都，雅典以伯里克利斯為首的艦隊介入，先不戰而取城，卻因島內階級反覆而再叛。海陸封鎖九個月後，薩米斯開城投降，雅典拆毀城牆、收繳艦隊。卡面埃及長矛並未隨軍而至，島上所用的卻是希臘重裝步兵的青銅矛。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 薩米安戰爭是雅典與薩米斯島城邦之間的一場戰爭，交戰地是東愛琴海上一座南北長約三十七公里的島嶼，島上主城隔馬卡萊海峽與小亞細亞本土相望，背後是愛琴海東岸的丘陵。薩米斯一方並非統一的國家：城邦政權分裂為寡頭與民主兩派，寡頭以土地為根基，掌控城防、艦隊與對外盟約；民主一派則倚靠港口、水手與商賈的人數。島上軍隊的核心是重裝步兵方陣與一支小型的三列槳戰艦隊，指揮權集中在少數家族手中，臨陣由寡頭首領直接調度，並無常設的將軍團。米利都是關鍵第三方：島上寡頭出亡後投奔米利都，米利都一度以武力送他們回島奪權，隨後又因懼怕雅典而轉向民主派，扮演了雙方之間的反覆者。科林斯與伯羅奔尼撒聯盟並未正式參戰，卻已備妥四十艘戰艦準備接應薩米斯，說明島上叛亂在雅典眼中已屬聯盟體系與科林斯之間的爭端。雅典一方是提洛同盟的盟主，自居希臘城邦的宗主，部隊由公民重裝步兵、艦上登岸兵與划槍手組成，指揮系統是每年抽籤選出的十人將軍委員會，戰時由其中一人統率。雙方實力對比懸殊：薩米斯有城牆、有港口、有島民的消耗能力，雅典有數十艘戰艦與久經圍城的經驗，勝負從一開始就偏向海權一方。
countriesEn: The Samian War was fought between Athens and the city-state of Samos, on an island of the eastern Aegean some thirty-seven kilometres long from north to south; the city on the island faces the strait of Mycale across the water from the mainland of Asia Minor, with the hills of the eastern Aegean coast rising behind it. The Samian side was not a unified state: the politics of the city split between an oligarchy and a demos. The oligarchy rested on landholding and controlled the defences of the island, its fleet and its foreign engagements; the democratic party leaned instead on the numbers of the harbour, the seamen and the merchants. The core of the island's military was a phalanx of hoplites and a small squadron of triremes, and command was concentrated in a few families and exercised directly by the leading oligarchs in the field, with no standing college of generals. Miletus was the decisive third party: after the island's oligarchs had been expelled they took refuge in Miletus, and Miletus put them back on the island by force, then, frightened of Athens, swung over to the democratic party, and served as a turncoat between the two sides. Corinth and the Peloponnesian League never fought in the war, but they had forty ships ready to bring aid to Samos, which shows that the island's revolt was already understood in Athens as a quarrel between the alliance system and Corinth. The Athenian side was the hegemon of the Delian League and claimed to stand as father of the Greek cities; its forces were composed of citizen hoplites, marines and oarsmen, and its command system was the board of ten generals chosen by lot each year, of whom one held command in the field. The balance of strength was lopsided: Samos had walls, a harbour and the endurance of an island population, while Athens had several dozen triremes and long experience of sieges, and from the outset the odds lay with the naval power.
people: 留下姓名的關鍵人物只有一位，就是伯里克利斯。他是雅典的將軍，這場戰爭前半段的仲裁者與後半段的統帥都是他。修昔底德記載，島上兩派爭執不下，雅典派出四十艘戰艦，由伯里克利斯與其餘將軍同往；伯里克利斯登島後把守城之權交給寡頭，只留一支小部隊便折返雅典，認定事情已了——正是這次過早撤離，成為往後全面叛亂的關鍵。他的第二次出現是率軍回師，接管城市、圍城九個月，直到薩米斯投降。伯里克利斯與薩米斯的關係早於這場戰爭：他的母親阿加里斯忒出自薩米斯豪族，僭主波利克瑞底斯之女又嫁給他的兒子克桑提波斯，兩家是姻親；這層私人關係使他在島上的仲裁既被信任，也被牽掛。島上兩派多數沒有留下名字，作用卻同樣關鍵：出亡的寡頭先後兩次翻案，一次引米利都入島，一次把城市交給科林斯；堅持召雅典入援的民主派，才是整場衝突真正的發起者。米利都人在島上充當了僱傭式的助力，兩度改換立場。雅典將軍委員會中的其餘成員負責實際圍城，文本未逐一具名。科林斯人只是備好艦隊等著接應，卻被雅典的巡邏擋在海峽之外。薩米斯降約與其後「薩米斯人是否編入雅典公民」的提案，在修昔底德筆下成為有名論辯，提案最終未能成行。
peopleEn: Only one key figure in this war left a name: Pericles. He was one of the Athenian generals, and he was both the arbiter of the first half of the affair and the commander of the second. Thucydides records that the two parties on the island could not settle their quarrel, that Athens sent out forty ships with Pericles and the other generals, and that Pericles, having taken possession of the city, handed the authority over it to the oligarchs, left behind a small body of troops and sailed back to Athens, convinced that the matter was settled. It was that premature withdrawal which became the hinge of the later general revolt. His second appearance was with the fleet returning, taking the city in hand and pressing the siege for nine months until Samos surrendered. Pericles' connection with Samos went back before the war itself: his mother Agariste came from a Samian house, and the daughter of the tyrant Polycrates was married to his son Xanthippus, so that the two families were bound by marriage. That private tie made him both trusted and beholden on the island. Most of the island's two parties left no names, yet they were equally decisive: the exiled oligarchs turned the tables twice, once bringing Miletus onto the island and once handing the city over to Corinth, while the democratic party that insisted on calling in Athens was the real origin of the whole conflict. The Milesians acted on the island as hired helpers and changed sides twice. The rest of the board of generals conducted the actual siege, and the text does not name them one by one. The Corinthians simply got their fleet ready to receive the island and were kept out of the strait by Athenian patrols. The terms of the Samian surrender, and the later proposal to enroll the Samians among the Athenians, became a recorded debate in Thucydides, and the proposal was never carried out.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛並沒有出現在薩米斯島上，把它放進這場戰爭的裝備表，是因為它標示了「金屬矛頭安在木柄上」這條技術路線最古老的源頭。卡片所記的是早王朝的形態：銅或青銅矛頭與木杆相接，用來守城垣，也用來收復失地；不過存世的實物標本以中王國之後最為齊備，早王朝更常見的反而是投擲棒一類的投射兵器。埃及真正的長矛大軍成形於新王國時代，戰車上的兩名乘員分別是弓手與持矛者，矛由此成為進攻與封鎖的常備兵器。薩米斯島上真正裝備在士兵手上的，是希臘重裝步兵的長矛：青銅矛頭近三葉形，套口安在白蠍木柄的末端，全長約兩米，每名重裝步兵通常備兩支，一支用於投擲，一支用於近身捅刺；盾牆排開之後，矛尖從圓盾的側後方伸出，抵住盾牌本身的重量。配套的還有青銅面圓盾、青銅胸甲、頭盔與短劍。攻城一方靠的是海軍：三列槳戰艦按修昔底德的記載有一百七十名划槍手，每一橫排座板上坐五十人，另有登岸兵自跳板衝上灘頭；步兵方面備有攻城梯、木製撞槌，以及填壕用的柴捆與土袋。島上的防禦設施同樣要緊：波利克瑞底斯修築的防波堤長約一千三百七十米，把城與港口連成一體；埃瓦利諾斯引水隧道長約一公里，把山泉引入城中，圍城方要真正斷水並不容易。運輸與補給則靠雙耳陶罐裝的油、酒與穀物，以及船隊在島與海峽之間的往返。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card never appeared on the island of Samos; it belongs in the equipment table of this war because it marks the oldest beginning of the line of technique in which a metal head is fixed to a wooden shaft. What the card records is the early dynastic form: a copper or bronze head joined to a wooden shaft, used to hold a wall and later to recover lost ground. It should be said, however, that the surviving specimens are much more complete from the Middle Kingdom onwards, while in the early dynastic period the throwstick and other missile weapons are the more usual find. The real Egyptian spear formations took shape in the New Kingdom, when the two men in a war chariot were the archer and the spear-bearer, and the spear became a standing weapon of assault and of blockade. The weapon actually in the hands of the soldiers of Samos was the spear of the Greek hoplite: a bronze head of almost three-lobed form, its socket fitted to the butt of an ash shaft, the whole weapon about two metres long, with two of them normally carried by each hoplite, one for throwing and one for thrusting at close quarters; once the shield wall was formed, the points came out behind and to the side of the round shields, taking the weight of the shields themselves. The rest of the kit was the bronze-faced round shield, the bronze cuirass, the helmet and the short sword. The besiegers relied on their navy: a trireme carried, on Thucydides' reckoning, one hundred and seventy oarsmen, fifty of them on each transverse row, and marines came ashore from the boarding bridges; on foot they had scaling ladders, wooden rams, and faggots and sacks of earth for filling the ditch. The island's own defences mattered just as much: the mole built by Polycrates runs for about one thousand three hundred and seventy metres and binds the city to its harbour together, while the water tunnel of Eupalinos, about a kilometre long, brings spring water into the city, so that cutting the water supply properly was no easy matter for the besiegers. Transport and supply rested on oil, wine and grain carried in amphorae with two handles, and on the shuttle of the fleet between the island and the strait.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術可以分成三段。第一段是不戰而取：雅典艦隊抵達後，島上寡頭與民主派議定把城市交給雅典，伯里克利斯登陸接管，留守少數人馬後即撤回，行動快到沒有留下任何攻城準備的痕跡。第二段是島內的反反覆覆：出亡的寡頭與米利都人合謀，把城市交給科林斯與伯羅奔尼撒人；民主派聞訊先一步起事，把寡頭再度逐出，雅典海軍及時趕到，圍城自此開始。第三段是長期的封鎖：雅典人沒有急著強攻，而是在島北與海峽一線建立海上封鎖，同時登陸設點，切斷陸路與季節性貨船的補給，把戰爭拖成一場消耗。修昔底德記錄的九個月圍城，關鍵在糧食：島上耕地有限，鹽、穀物與燃料都靠外運，冬季風季東愛琴海航運減緩，守軍的儲糧在夏末之後便開始見底。守方曾試圖以城內出擊與科林斯接應扭轉局面，卻因艦隊被封而難以出港。攻城方也留了餘地：最後的結束不是強攻破城，而是以明確條件換取投降，拆毀城牆、交出人質、繳交艦隊、支付戰費。重裝步兵在此役中沒有正面對決的機會，決定勝負的是艦隊、封鎖線與時間——誰能撐得久，誰就贏。
tacticsEn: The course of this war falls into three stages. The first is the taking of the city without a fight: when the Athenian fleet arrived, the oligarchs and the democratic party agreed to hand the city over, Pericles landed and took possession, and he withdrew with only a small body left behind, so quickly that no trace of any preparation for a siege was left. The second is the turning back and forth inside the island: the exiled oligarchs plotted with the Milesians to hand the city to the Corinthians and the Peloponnesians; the democratic party, hearing of it, rose first and drove the oligarchs out once more; and the Athenian fleet arrived in time, and the siege began. The third is the long blockade: the Athenians did not hurry to assault, but established a blockade by sea to the north of the island and along the strait, and at the same time landed and held posts that cut the land route and the seasonal shipping, dragging the war out into a contest of endurance. The nine months of siege that Thucydides records turn on food: the island has little arable land, and salt, grain and fuel all came in by sea, while the winter winds slow the shipping of the eastern Aegean, so that the defenders' stock of provisions began to run short from the end of summer onwards. The defenders tried to reverse their position by sorties from the city and by a relief from Corinth, but the blockade kept their ships in the harbour. The besiegers, for their part, left themselves room: the end was not the storming of the walls but a surrender negotiated on explicit terms, the walls to be razed, hostages to be given, the ships to be handed over and the cost of the war to be paid. The hoplites of the two sides never had the chance of a set-piece collision; what decided the war was the fleet, the line of blockade and time, and whoever could hold out the longer was the winner.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是文本自述：戰爭年份為前440年，圍城歷時九個月，投降在次年冬春之交（通行定於前439年）；修昔底德記雅典為平定薩米斯派出四十艘戰艦，同書另記伯里克利斯此前赴赫勒斯滂攻取塞斯托斯時用兵五十艘；科林斯準備接應薩米斯的艦隊亦為四十艘；希羅多德《歷史》第三卷記載，在更早的島上風波中，波利克瑞底斯曾以一百艘五十人划槳船與一千名重裝步兵平定起義，這是薩米斯軍力的一個早期尺度。第二類是地理與考古：全島南北長約三十七公里，最寬處約十公里，面積約四百八十平方公里，與馬卡萊海峽最近處約六公里；波利克瑞底斯的防波堤長約一千三百七十米；埃瓦利諾斯引水隧道長約一公里。修昔底德《歷史》2.22 記三列槳戰艦每艦划槍手一百七十人、每排座板五十人，可據以估算封鎖艦隊的人力消耗與淡水需求。第三類是必須打折扣的推估：圍城九個月的守軍人數沒有任何可靠數字可考，多數研究只能說是足以守城的重裝步兵與登岸兵；島上人口與常備兵力的估算範圍寬廣，差距可達數倍。薩米斯在提洛同盟貢賦表上以「薩米斯人」的名義出現，可見它是同盟成員，卻不等於知道它實際繳付的數目。戰爭的實際損耗數字，兩造都沒有留下記錄。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is what the texts say of themselves. The year of the war is 440 BC; the siege lasted nine months, and the surrender came in the winter and spring that followed, conventionally dated to 439 BC. Thucydides records that Athens sent forty ships to reduce Samos, and in the same book that Pericles had taken fifty ships to the Hellespont to seize Sestos not long before; the fleet that Corinth prepared to bring aid to Samos was likewise of forty ships. Herodotus, in the third book of the Histories, records that in an earlier disturbance on the island Polycrates had put down a revolt with a hundred pentekonters and a thousand hoplites, and that is one early measure of Samian military strength. The second class is geography and archaeology: the island is about thirty-seven kilometres from north to south and about ten kilometres at its widest, with an area of roughly four hundred and eighty square kilometres, and the narrowest reach of the strait of Mycale is about six kilometres away; the mole of Polycrates runs for some one thousand three hundred and seventy metres; the water tunnel of Eupalinos is about a kilometre long. Thucydides at 2.22 gives one hundred and seventy oarsmen to a trireme, fifty to each transverse row, from which the manning and the water demands of a blockading fleet can be estimated. The third class is estimate, and must be discounted: no reliable figure survives for the size of the garrison during the nine months, and most studies can only speak of hoplites and marines sufficient to man the walls; estimates of the island's population and standing forces range widely and differ by a factor of several. Samos appears in the tribute lists of the Delian League under the name of the Samians, which shows it was a member of the alliance, but does not tell us the sum it actually paid. Neither side left any record of the actual losses of the war.
cause: 打起來的原因可以分四層。最表層是島上的階級鬥爭：寡頭與民主派勢不兩立，民主派一度驅逐寡頭，出亡的寡頭便向外求助。第二層是米利都的介入：這座曾被雅典鎮壓、才在不久前重歸同盟秩序的城邦，出於自身對雅典的不滿，也出於島上航運與鹽業的爭端，插手薩米斯內政，把島上反雅典的棋子放上棋盤。第三層是雅典的帝國邏輯：薩米斯是提洛同盟的成員，島上反叛若落到科林斯與伯羅奔尼撒聯盟手中，雅典失去的不只是一個城邦，而是東愛琴海通往赫勒斯滂與小亞細亞的門戶；前一年雅典才在赫勒斯滂攻下塞斯托斯，此時再讓薩米斯倒向科林斯，等於把前線拱手讓人。第四層是時機：前445年雅典與斯巴達訂下的五年和約正在有效期內，雅典在西部正與科林斯一系糾葛，陸軍可以抽調的餘裕有限，但海軍調度不成問題。遠因更早：波利克瑞底斯時代的薩米斯曾以海盜聞名，其後又數度脫離雅典控制，島上對雅典的疑心由來已久。於是一次島內的政變，最終演成了一場海權與城邦聯盟之間的戰爭。
causeEn: The reasons for the war can be set out in four layers. The outermost is the class struggle inside the island: the oligarchs and the democratic party were at daggers drawn, the democrats drove the oligarchs out on one occasion, and the exiled oligarchs turned outward for help. The second layer is the intervention of Miletus: a city that had itself been put down by Athens and had only lately been brought back into the order of the alliance, and which was both aggrieved at Athens and interested in the shipping and the salt trade of the island, meddled in the internal affairs of Samos and put an anti-Athenian piece on the board. The third layer is the logic of the Athenian empire: Samos was a member of the Delian League, and if the island's revolt fell into the hands of Corinth and the Peloponnesian League, Athens would lose not merely a city but the gateway of the eastern Aegean to the Hellespont and the mainland of Asia Minor; the year before, Athens had taken Sestos in the Hellespont, and to let Samos go over to Corinth now would be to hand over the front line. The fourth layer is timing: the five years' peace between Athens and Sparta struck in 445 BC was still in force, and Athens was already entangled with the Corinthian party in the west, so the margin for drawing off hoplites was thin, though moving the fleet was no problem at all. The remote cause is older still: under Polycrates the island had a reputation as a nest of pirates, and it had broken away from Athenian control more than once since; the suspicion of Athens in Samos was long-standing. A constitutional coup inside the island thus turned into a war between a naval power and a league of city-states.
impact: 這場戰爭沒有留下大戰役的痕跡，卻把雅典的海上霸權重新鑄了一遍。第一，帝國的處置方式成形：面對同盟成員的叛亂，雅典的做法不是靠野戰決勝負，而是海陸封鎖加上投降條件，並在城破之後拆毀城牆、收繳艦隊，使受罰的一方失去再叛的物質基礎；這套辦法在後來處置提洛同盟其他城邦時一再出現。第二，雅典干預同盟內政的模樣被固定下來：站在民主派一邊對抗本地寡頭，薩米斯之後，在米蒂利尼又重演一次，模式相同而手段更重。第三，薩米斯島的命運被定下：城牆夷平、艦隊繳械、主持叛亂的寡頭被處死，剩下的城邦成為雅典的附屬；至於是否把薩米斯人編入雅典公民、另立一個城區，提案在修昔底德筆下被否，其後是否另設屯田及其時間，學界至今仍有爭議，說明這場戰爭的善後從一開始就沒有定案。第四，與科林斯的關係惡化：科林斯四十艘戰艦的接應被擋在海峽之外，此事成為前431年雅典與伯羅奔尼撒聯盟全面開戰的前奏之一；伯里克利斯在葬禮演說中把平定薩米斯列為功績，同時又警告雅典人不要養成一條「戰爭之犬」，那段話本身就說明這場勝利在當時已被視為危險的勝利。第五，史料上的收穫：修昔底德《歷史》第一卷的記載是了解這場戰爭的主要依據，而島上的城牆遺址、防波堤與引水隧道，則為這座城邦的經濟與軍事部署提供了物質佐證。
impactEn: The war left no trace of a great battle, yet it recast the Athenian mastery of the sea. First, the empire's way of dealing with things was formed: faced with the revolt of a member of the alliance, Athens did not settle the matter by a battle in the field but by blockade on land and sea together with terms of surrender, and after the city fell she razed the walls and took the ships, so that the punished party was stripped of the material basis of any future rebellion. The same procedure was used again and again in the handling of other cities of the Delian League. Second, the pattern of Athenian interference in the internal affairs of the alliance was fixed: siding with the democratic party against the local oligarchy, as at Samos, and repeated later at Mytilene in the same pattern but with heavier hand. Third, the fate of the island of Samos was settled: the walls razed, the fleet confiscated, the oligarchs who had led the revolt put to death, and the remaining city left as a dependency of Athens. Whether the Samians should be enrolled among the Athenians as a new deme was proposed and rejected in Thucydides, and whether a cleruchy was established there afterwards, and when, is still disputed among scholars, which shows that the settlement of this war was never settled at all. Fourth, relations with Corinth soured: the relief of forty ships was kept out of the strait, and this became one of the preliminaries to the general war between Athens and the Peloponnesian League that began in 431 BC. Pericles claimed the reduction of Samos among the achievements of Athens in his funeral speech, while warning the Athenians not to rear a dog of war, and the speech itself shows that the victory was already regarded at the time as a dangerous one. Fifth, in terms of the record: the first book of Thucydides is the principal source for the war, while the walls, the mole and the water tunnel on the island supply material evidence for the economy and the military dispositions of the city.
result: 前440年夏末，雅典的封鎖線合攏；九個月後，薩米斯城中的糧食與燃料耗盡，守軍無法再撐，島方開城談判。降約的內容由修昔底德記下來，條目清楚：拆毀城牆、交付人質、繳出艦隊、支付戰爭費用。城破之後，主持叛亂的寡頭被處死，其餘居民依約處置，島上原有的艦隊不再存在，一支曾經在東愛琴海頗有名聲的海上力量自此在編制上消失。薩米斯作為提洛同盟成員的地位得以恢復，卻已不是原來的薩米斯；其後這座島在雅典的秩序裡維持了相當長時間，直到前431年之後的那場大戰把它捲入新的漩渦。關於善後，曾有人提議把薩米斯人編入雅典公民、另立一個城區，提案未獲通過。最後可以這樣總結：這場戰爭的勝負並不是由任何一場正面會戰決定的，而是由封鎖、飢餓與島內階級的算計共同決定的；它的歷史意義則在於把「同盟叛亂如何收拾」這道題目的答案，第一次以海軍加投降條件的形式寫了下來，寫給後來的人看。
resultEn: In the late summer of 440 BC the Athenian lines of blockade closed; nine months later the food and the fuel of the city of Samos were exhausted, the garrison could hold out no longer, and the island opened negotiations. Thucydides has left the terms of the surrender, and the items are clear: the walls to be razed, hostages to be given, the ships to be handed over, and the cost of the war to be paid. After the city fell, the oligarchs who had led the revolt were put to death, the rest of the inhabitants were dealt with according to the terms, and the island's own fleet ceased to exist, a maritime force that had once been spoken of with respect in the eastern Aegean disappearing from the order of battle. Samos recovered its standing as a member of the Delian League, but it was no longer the Samos it had been; the island then stayed for a long while in the Athenian order, until the great war after 431 BC drew it into new convulsions. As for the settlement, there was a proposal to enroll the Samians among the Athenians as a separate deme, and it was not carried. The result can finally be put in this way: the outcome of this war was decided not by any set-piece engagement but by blockade, hunger and the calculations of the island's factions, and its historical significance lies in having written down, for the first time and in the form of a fleet plus terms of surrender, the answer to the question of how a rebellious ally is to be dealt with, written down for those who came after.
